title: Review of the long Marangoni turnover run on fresh seed 83: with removed matter returned at once, rods keep dividing through frame 320 (50 persistent splits, 48 dividing tracks vs 16 without turnover), and the swim-3-lengths minority stays rare (2 of 48)
summary: The finding's world.py, 128^2, 400 frames (T=2000), seed 83, labkit; c00's extract.py and the finding's turnover_stats.py (40-frame windows) unchanged. p_dil 0.10 with REDIST: 40 removal events take 81 bodies; persistent splits 50, generation 5; splits per 40 frames 2, 6, 6, 8, 11, 3, 5, 9 through frame 320, then 0 (the last 20 frames cannot hold a persistent split under labkit's K=20 window); bodies plateau at 22-30; 48 dividing tracks, median D 1.30, 2 of 48 swim 3 rod lengths. No-dilution twin on the same seed: 34 persistent splits, generation 4, splits fall from 5-9 to 1-3 per 40 frames after frame 160, 16 dividing tracks (1 of 16 >= 3). Turnover with returned matter triples the number of dividing rods and keeps division going about twice as long; the far-swimming minority stays rare, as the finding says.

observations.D: runs/redist/stats.txt: 50 persistent splits, 2-11 per 40 frames to frame 320, 48 dividing tracks; runs/nodil/stats.txt: 34 splits, 1-3 per 40 frames after frame 160, 16 dividing tracks

seeds_run.result: pass: sustained division with REDIST (48 vs 16 dividing), minority 2 of 48 >= 3 rod lengths

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; I did not run the mar=0 floor or the parent-offspring regression, so the 'redrawn every cycle' part is not re-tested here. The births per removal are below 1 (50 splits for 81 removals); body numbers hold because the returned matter also nucleates new rods (merges_born and nucleations not separated in stats.txt).
